rule: GOAL: Guide the purple square along the dotted path to the blue target circle. CONTROLS: Click the white cross marker to move the square to that position. RULE: The square only advances when you click the specific cross icon ahead of it. TRAP: Clicking other path dots or distant targets does nothing; you must find and click the cross.

GOAL: Find the shortest path through a maze of rooms to reach the exit marker. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move between adjacent rooms, only passing through open doors. RULE: Only gray doors are open; black walls block movement between rooms. TRAP: Assuming you can slide along walls or pass through closed black doors wastes actions.

GOAL: Move three large blocks into their matching blue target frames. CONTROLS: Arrows move your character; Space picks up or drops the block you face. RULE: You automatically face the block directly ahead when you stop next to it. TRAP: Pressing Space without facing a block does nothing; ensure you are adjacent before acting.

GOAL: Guide the falling block to rest inside the cup notch. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the red bar; spacebar releases the block. RULE: The block bounces off the bar to steer into the target. TRAP: Covering the cup with paint does not win; the block must land and stay inside.

GOAL: Align the handle's yellow section with the bar's gap to complete the connection. CONTROLS: The two blue buttons shift the handle left or right in fixed steps. RULE: Precise alignment of the specific yellow shapes triggers the win condition. TRAP: Assuming the gray area needs to cover the blue buttons wastes time; only the yellow parts matter.

GOAL: Set all toggle switches to the black state. CONTROLS: Click individual switch slots to change their color from gray to black. RULE: The level is solved only when every single switch is black. TRAP: Assuming the switch color is decorative; it is the actual state of the circuit.

GOAL: Align the gray handle with the gap by moving two bars down. CONTROLS: Click below the lower bar to move it down; click below the upper bar to raise the lower bar. RULE: The lower bar cannot move down if the upper bar is already at its lowest position. TRAP: Thinking you can push the lower bar down indefinitely; you must first raise the upper bar to free space.

GOAL: Extend both bars to touch their matching plus signs. CONTROLS: Click a bar to stretch it one unit right. RULE: Each bar grows independently; both must connect to their specific plus to win. TRAP: Believing one connection ends the level; you must satisfy both targets within the click limit.

GOAL: Align the plug’s tip with the socket to close the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the plug left and right along the track. RULE: Each press shifted the plug exactly four units, overriding the automatic drift. TRAP: Ignoring the slow leftward drift caused overshooting; constant adjustment was required to stay centered.

GOAL: Rotate five glyphs to match reference shapes. CONTROLS: Left/Right arrows move cursor between slots; Up arrow rotates the selected glyph. RULE: Each slot cycles through eight distinct orientations; stop when the shape aligns with the target. TRAP: Assuming a single correct rotation exists wastes time, as multiple symmetrical orientations may satisfy the match condition.

GOAL: Reach the exit without getting caught. CONTROLS: Arrows move one step. RULE: The red enemy lunges two spaces toward you if you enter its range. TRAP: Believing you can dodge mid-lunge; once triggered, the strike is unavoidable, so never step within its threat zone.

GOAL: Shrink the wide plug tip to a 2x2 square so it fits through the narrow charcoal neck to reach the head. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the tip along the vertical track; clicking the three yellow keypad cells triggers the shrink. RULE: Completing the keypad pattern toggles the tip's size, shrinking it to pass through constrictions. TRAP: Assuming rotation helps; the key is shrinking the tip via the keypad, not rotating or widening it.

GOAL: Slide four vertical walls to align their edges with specific target rows. CONTROLS: Clicking a wall shifts it and its neighbor two units in opposite directions. RULE: Each click adjusts two adjacent walls, so total displacement is conserved across pairs. TRAP: Assuming walls move independently wastes moves; you must plan paired shifts to hit all targets simultaneously.

ESTABLISHED: The wire passes through blocks, pulling them left when retracted. Vertical movement requires coupling, but horizontal pushing seems to break the connection, leaving a gap. FAILED: Attempting to move blocks vertically by coupling them first, then moving the player up or down, did not transport the block to the new row. GOAL IS NOT: Simply dragging a block to a target coordinate while maintaining a continuous wire connection from the player. CONTROLS: Left pulls coupled blocks. Right extends the wire. Up and Down move the player without moving coupled blocks.

GOAL: Clear the grid by navigating through enemies without dying in 19 moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blue tile one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Entering an enemy's tile consumes it only if no other enemy can attack you. TRAP: Assuming all adjacent enemies are safe; a second enemy lunging along the row caused death.

GOAL: Match the pink row's shapes to the yellow row by finding the correct identity in each slot's cycle. CONTROLS: Use arrow keys to move the cursor between slots and cycle through available shape options. RULE: Each slot contains a fixed set of shape identities; find the one matching the required pair family. TRAP: Assuming rotation matters; the match is based on shape identity, not the specific rotation displayed.

GOAL: Connect the plug to the head to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug; the keypad sends power once connected. RULE: The plug must physically touch the head before pressing the keypad. TRAP: Assuming the connection triggers a win automatically; you must manually activate the switch.

GOAL: Decode a seven-slot word by matching shapes, not just identities. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate glyphs to find the correct shape variant for each slot. RULE: A shape counts as a match if it belongs to the same visual family, even if rotated. TRAP: Demanding an exact pixel-perfect rotation instead of accepting any shape in the family wastes moves.

GOAL: Make the main grid match the small pattern shown in its center. CONTROLS: Click a grid cell to toggle its color. RULE: Each cell in the main grid must take the color of the corresponding cell in the center mini-map. TRAP: Thinking the center mini-map updates live as you play; it is a fixed target.

GOAL: Align the plug's prongs with the socket pins to close the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug; Space rotates it. RULE: The plug only moves three spaces per arrow press. TRAP: Assuming the plug stops when touching pins; it stops one space short, requiring precise alignment before contact.

GOAL: Turn all required grid cells orange to match the mini-pattern targets. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to toggle their color between blue and orange. RULE: Cells shown white in the mini-pattern must be orange; gray cells remain blue. TRAP: Believing the mini-pattern center color dictates the starting state rather than the target color.

GOAL: Place the gray shape inside the ring by aligning the white and gray centers symmetrically. CONTROLS: Click an empty spot to move the white piece; click the gray piece to swap positions. RULE: The game checks if the midpoint between the two pieces matches the ring’s center. TRAP: Thinking the gray piece could be moved directly; it only reacts to swaps or acts as a static anchor.

GOAL: Match tile shapes by pairing columns and verifying connectivity across rows. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor to select and swap tiles. RULE: Two tiles match only if one is a rotation or reflection of the other. TRAP: Assuming visual similarity is enough; ignoring exact symmetry checks led to failed links.

ESTABLISHED: Three cups fill using specific bar placements; geometry allows split paths to reach all targets. FAILED: Placing the wide bar at columns 28-47 or the narrow bar at 24-35 blocks critical risers, causing dead ends or missed cups. GOAL IS NOT: A simple single-shot solution; it requires precise multi-step splitting where bars redirect flows without blocking necessary upward paths. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move bars; Space drops them; Z undoes the last move; R resets the level.

GOAL: Determine each cell's target color using the four mini grids to complete the pattern. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle their color between red and orange. RULE: White pixels match the mini's center color; gray pixels match the opposite color. TRAP: Assuming the mapping is fixed; it actually flips based on whether the mini's center is red or orange.

GOAL: Traverse the grid to the exit while dodging a patrolling orange enemy. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per press. RULE: The enemy moves predictably; timing your steps to avoid its current location ensures safety. TRAP: Assuming you can safely step onto the enemy's current tile or bypass its path without waiting.

GOAL: Paint the left side purple and the top white. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the brush along the hexagon edge; Space stamps the selected color. RULE: Keys follow the path: Left then Down reaches the west point; Up then Right returns to the top. TRAP: Assuming keys are absolute directions causes you to move away from the target instead of along the perimeter.

GOAL: Set every grid cell to match the hidden target color. CONTROLS: Tapping a cell cycles it through three colors. RULE: A mini-grid is solved when its outer cells are not blue. TRAP: Assuming a tap just toggles two colors; it actually cycles three, so you must count taps carefully to land on the correct hue.

ESTABLISHED: The two dots move independently within a ring-shaped maze. FAILED: Placing dots in narrow passages, making them adjacent, or moving them to outer corners did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Cutting the ring's path, locking dots in necks, or simply spreading them to opposite corners. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active dot; switching active dots changes which one responds to input.

GOAL: Match the target pattern using four specific stamps. CONTROLS: Click color buttons to select paint. Spacebar stamps the current region. Arrow keys move the mold. RULE: Each stamp paints a fixed geometric shape, like a half-plane or triangle, overwriting previous colors. TRAP: Assuming stamps are additive. They are not; later stamps erase earlier colors in their region, so order matters critically.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding moving sentries. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move you one step. RULE: You move first, then sentries move along their fixed paths. TRAP: Assuming sentries stop at edges; they bounce back and forth continuously.

GOAL: Move two dots to specific target cells. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active dot. RULE: Only one dot moves per press; the other stays fixed. TRAP: Assuming both dots move together or that a single move shifts the whole group.

GOAL: Guide the tip to the exit by shrinking, navigating, and growing at the end. CONTROLS: Arrows move; diamond clicks shrink or grow; middle clicks trigger burnout. RULE: Burnout only works when the tip is inside the gray arm facing the socket. TRAP: Running out of energy causes instant death, so plan the full route before moving.

ESTABLISHED: Light gray segments mark target levels for gray flow. Plugs open when levels align with segment bottoms. FAILED: Trying to force alignment on the yellow plug without adjusting gray levels first. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching light gray segment bottoms immediately. CONTROLS: Presses raise bar levels. Handle moves between bands. Gray flows when levels match segment ranges.

GOAL: Paint the grid using overlapping diagonal rules to satisfy color constraints. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor; clicks select colors; space stamps the pattern. RULE: Later stamps overwrite earlier ones, so apply diagonal constraints in the correct order. TRAP: Believing colors mix additively; they replace, so wrong ordering ruins previous work.

GOAL: Place the start and end markers to link the rope without crossing water. CONTROLS: Click a cell to move the start or end marker. RULE: Every pixel of the marker’s shape must stay inside the playable area, never touching the gray border. TRAP: Assuming the center point was valid even if the marker’s edges spilled over the boundary.

GOAL: Transform the grid colors to match the target pattern derived from the mini-hints. CONTROLS: Clicking a plain cell flips its own color; clicking a checker cell flips itself and its four neighbors. RULE: A 'W' marker means use the mini’s center color, while a 'g' marker means use the other color. TRAP: Assuming checker clicks only affect neighbors, forgetting they also toggle the checker cell itself.

GOAL: Paint the board in four specific colors by stamping a large area then a small block. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor; Space stamps the selected color; mouse clicks select colors or place small blocks. RULE: New colors completely overwrite previous ones, so order matters most: big shapes first, details last. TRAP: Thinking you must erase or toggle colors wastes time; just stamp the final color directly over any mistakes.

ESTABLISHED: The red bar toggles between horizontal and vertical positions. The blue block toggles between two distinct locations. These single toggles prevent a continuous path from the start box to the yellow core. FAILED: Clicking the blue hat repeatedly only cycles between two known states. Clicking the red hat repeatedly only cycles between two known states. Neither action creates a third state or simultaneous bridge. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the yellow core with current toggle mechanics. The puzzle is not solved by simple alternating clicks. The goal requires discovering a hidden state or m

GOAL: Stamp four colors in a fixed order to fill a grid. CONTROLS: Arrows move the mold; clicks select tools or confirm stamps. RULE: The stamp order is strict; you cannot change the sequence. TRAP: Assuming you can pick the shortest path between stamps; the fixed order forces a longer route.

GOAL: Position the ball on the target zone to complete the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the ball; mouse clicks reposition structural blocks. RULE: Only specific colored tiles allow the ball to rest; others are solid barriers. TRAP: Assuming the checkerboard pattern was passable wasted time; it blocks movement completely.

GOAL: Move the cursor to the target column and adjust the glyph to the required pose. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows move the cursor; up and down arrows rotate the current glyph. RULE: The cursor stays on the active column until you explicitly move it; rotation is modular. TRAP: Assuming the cursor advances automatically after solving a column wastes actions on redundant moves.

GOAL: Fill the designated cups with falling blocks to complete the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block horizontally; spacebar drops it instantly. RULE: Blocks split into clones when hitting the bar, filling multiple cups at once. TRAP: Assuming mass is conserved; you must account for cloning mechanics, not simple physics.

GOAL: Place the midpoint between the white and gray tokens directly onto the center of the ring. CONTROLS: Clicking an empty square moves the white token there. Clicking the gray token swaps its position with the white one. RULE: The game tracks the exact midpoint of the two tokens, not their individual locations, as the winning condition. TRAP: Believing you must move a single token onto the ring wastes turns; you must manipulate both tokens to position the invisible center point.

GOAL: Shrink the plug to fit the narrow track and slide it fully into the left socket. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the plug; clicking painted cells to reduce its size. RULE: The plug must be narrow enough to pass through the upper channel before insertion. TRAP: Assuming the original size could fit; ignoring the need to shrink it first wasted time.

GOAL: Guide the ball to the yellow core. CONTROLS: Arrows move the ball; buttons rotate bars. RULE: Rotating the red bar creates a bridge to the yellow zone. TRAP: Moving straight up fails; you must rotate the red bar to connect the paths.

ESTABLISHED: The budget bar is visibly depleted and nearing empty. The white object is active; the blue U-shape is purple. FAILED: Clicking the yellow and the plug did not clear the level or reduce the cost. GOAL IS NOT: Simply making objects white or swapping active states does not solve the puzzle. CONTROLS: Clicking an object makes it active (white) and turns the previous active object purple.

GOAL: Rotate seven glyph rings to match a specific target sequence of shapes derived from word pairs. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotated the selected ring forward or backward through its cycle of shapes. RULE: Only the shape’s rotational class mattered; exact orientation was irrelevant as long as the class matched the target. TRAP: Believing that specific starting poses required precise alignment, wasting actions on unnecessary rotations instead of checking class matches.

GOAL: Clear white cells to shrink the plug, then push it up through the narrow shaft to the head. CONTROLS: Click white cells to erase them; use arrow keys to move the plug. RULE: The plug only fits the gap after you clear every white cell, causing it to shrink. TRAP: Do not try to push the plug before clearing all white cells; it is too wide and will jam.

GOAL: Guide two dots to a direct swap in the same row to win. CONTROLS: Arrows move the left dot normally; the right dot mirrors every move. RULE: If both dots target the same empty cell, they stay put, blocking progress. TRAP: Assuming vertical adjacency allows a swap; mirrored controls only permit horizontal swaps.

GOAL: Navigate the maze to consume all red enemies while avoiding their attack cones. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player one room in the chosen direction. RULE: Red enemies only attacked the single room directly in front of them, allowing safe movement through their flanks. TRAP: Assuming enemies attacked at distance two wasted time waiting for a safe path that did not exist.

GOAL: Decode a hidden message by mapping yellow symbols to blue words using a dictionary, then correct the blue row. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor and cycle through symbol classes; UP rotates the current symbol’s identity. RULE: Each yellow word uniquely maps to a blue word; the bottom row must match these mapped values exactly. TRAP: Assuming symbols map directly by shape rather than by their cyclic class order, causing misaligned translations.

GOAL: Align the yellow row to match the chained translation targets derived from the source symbols. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cursor and cycled the current symbol through its available options. RULE: Source symbols map to intermediate symbols, which then map to the final yellow targets in a strict chain. TRAP: Assuming direct source-to-target mapping ignored the necessary intermediate step, causing repeated misalignments.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding the slow-moving chaser. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one room per turn. RULE: Maintain a distance of two or more by always moving to a node farther from the chaser. TRAP: Assuming the chaser moves every turn like you. It moves slower, so do not rush; move deliberately to keep your lead.

GOAL: Move the green rope ends to form a specific knot shape while avoiding the purple rope's center. CONTROLS: Click an end to select it, then click a valid cell to move it. RULE: The knot’s shape must not overlap the center of any rope end, including the other color’s. TRAP: Assuming only your own rope’s ends block the knot; ignoring the opponent’s center caused invalid moves.

GOAL: Replicate the small static target pattern shown in the mini grid. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles its color between red and blue. RULE: White pixels in the mini grid indicate red cells; gray pixels indicate blue cells. TRAP: Assuming the mini grid updates dynamically with your clicks, when it actually remains fixed as a reference.

GOAL: Match the grid pattern to the target displays shown in the mini grids. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle their color between blue and orange. RULE: Each mini grid dictates the required color for its specific three-by-three section of the main board. TRAP: Assuming the mini grids were independent clues rather than strict blueprints for overlapping sections, causing wasted toggles.

GOAL: Guide the ball to the yellow core. CONTROLS: Arrows move the ball; clicks toggle colors. RULE: Only solid colors block movement; transparent ones allow passage. TRAP: Thinking all purple zones are solid; toggling one affects all purple areas globally.

GOAL: Cycle the two-symbol tiles to match the target word's rendered glyphs. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the tile's state through its fixed sequence of symbol pairs. RULE: Each tile cycles through a specific set of seven symbol classes, rendering pairs based on that class. TRAP: Assuming the raw symbol pair alone determines the state; the specific rendering pose of the class matters for the match.

GOAL: Turn the grid orange by painting cells that match each mini's center color. CONTROLS: Click individual cells to toggle their color between red and orange. RULE: A cell becomes orange if its color matches the center color of its covering mini. TRAP: Assuming all cells need manual painting; mini centers are fixed and should not be clicked.

GOAL: Move each blob to the ring matching its color. CONTROLS: Click to grab a blob; click again to place it. RULE: Only same-color blobs complete their rings; mixed pairs fail. TRAP: Thinking any blob fits any ring wastes turns on invalid moves.

GOAL: Slide both blocks into the top corridor until they touch in the middle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the left block normally and the right block in the opposite direction. RULE: The right block mirrors your input, so pressing Left pushes it right. TRAP: Assuming both blocks move the same way wastes turns fighting against the mirror control.

GOAL: Place all ends on dry land without overlapping other objects. CONTROLS: Click to drop a piece; drag to rotate it before releasing. RULE: The four corners of every piece must touch solid ground, not water or wires. TRAP: Assuming the center point determines placement; ignoring the corners causes immediate rejection.

GOAL: Turn specific grid cells orange to match the pattern. CONTROLS: Click a cell to cycle its color through blue, red, and orange. RULE: Each click advances the color one step in the fixed cycle. TRAP: Assuming the progress bar measures click limits, when it actually tracks elapsed time.

GOAL: Move the N blob to (53,55) and the P blob to (57,34). CONTROLS: Click to swap the cursor with a nearby piece; click again to move the cursor to a new position. RULE: Each click on a new cell replaces the piece under the cursor with that cell's piece, shifting the group's average position. TRAP: Trying to move pieces one by one; you must plan the final average, not the path.

GOAL: Navigate two dots through a maze to make them adjacent. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both dots simultaneously in that direction. RULE: The rightmost dot mirrors any vertical movement while the left moves normally. TRAP: Assuming symmetric movement causes collisions; you must account for the mirror rule to avoid blocking paths.

GOAL: Split the block horizontally with a purple bottom and white top. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the pour angle; mouse clicks select the paint color; spacebar pours. RULE: The pour angle dictates which half receives paint, so align the cup to the top half before pouring. TRAP: Assuming the cup position was already correct for the final pour, causing wasted actions trying to paint the wrong section.

ESTABLISHED: Three blocks reached all three cups, yet the level ended in failure. FAILED: Filling every cup completely did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply filling all available cups to win. CONTROLS: Moving bars shifts obstacles; placing bars creates barriers that split falling blocks into multiple pieces.

GOAL: Swap the positions of the two blocks to clear the path. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both blocks simultaneously, but one block moves in the opposite direction. RULE: When the blocks move toward each other, they pass through and swap places instead of blocking. TRAP: Believing the blocks would stop each other upon collision, causing unnecessary detours.

ESTABLISHED: A 6x6 gray board with a green center exists. Two podiums (red and blue) sit on the right. Clicking podiums removes white outlines and shifts piece orientation. FAILED: Various knob positions and clicks did not trigger a win. No specific sequence or joystick direction combination solved the puzzle. GOAL IS NOT: The podiums are not just color targets, nor are they simple shape templates for the left-side pieces. CONTROLS: The knob toggles piece orientation (vertical/horizontal). Clicking podiums removes outlines but does not insert pieces.

GOAL: Slide the plug to touch the socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug three spaces per press; SPACE resets position. RULE: Movement is chunky, not smooth, so count steps in threes to align the plug perfectly. TRAP: Thinking arrows move one space causes overshooting and wasted time recalculating positions.

GOAL: Turn every grid cell to N while ignoring the legend. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle colors; click minis to change their state. RULE: The top-right legend is not part of the puzzle grid. TRAP: Treating the legend as a playable cell forces impossible moves and wastes clicks.

GOAL: Match colored blobs to rings by exact color sets. CONTROLS: Click rings to assign blobs. RULE: A ring is valid only if its colors exactly match a blob’s colors. TRAP: Thinking swaps move cells between groups; they don’t, only ownership changes, so group positions stay fixed.

GOAL: Fill the lower channel completely, then move the ball right across the solid floor to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the ball; clicks shifted a horizontal bar or advanced fluid flow. RULE: The ball can only cross the gap when the entire row below is solid material. TRAP: Moving the ball down too early trapped it on unstable ground; wait for full saturation before descending.

GOAL: Create a white zone where rows are low and sums are low. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the pour angle; clicks select paint; space pours. RULE: Later pours overwrite earlier ones, so paint the largest area last. TRAP: Thinking order doesn't matter; pouring the full orange zone first hides the purple, making the white gap impossible.

GOAL: Swap two dots by moving one while the other stays blocked. CONTROLS: Arrows move both dots simultaneously, unless one is blocked. RULE: A dot stops moving if it hits a wall or a placed marker. TRAP: Assuming both dots always move; placing a marker blocks one, allowing independent control.

GOAL: Fill the grid by pouring colored liquids through rotated directions and stamping a final pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the cup; Space pours liquid; Mouse selects colors or stamps the bottle. RULE: Each rotation changes where the liquid flows, so align the cup to hit specific grid regions. TRAP: Rotating the cup moves the bottle, so stamping at the wrong angle lands the pattern in the wrong spot.

GOAL: Align the yellow plug with the wall gap by shifting the gray shape. CONTROLS: Clicking blue blocks expands one gray section while contracting the other. RULE: The gray region maintains constant area, acting like a piston between two halves. TRAP: Assuming the blue blocks move physically; they actually control the gray shape's internal balance.

GOAL: Fill regions by rotating a bottle to pour specific colors into matching zones. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the bottle; clicks select paint colors or trigger pours and stamps. RULE: Rotating changes which grid half receives paint; a final stamp applies a pattern at the current angle. TRAP: Assuming rotation direction is arbitrary; precise clockwise or counter-clockwise steps are required to align pours and stamps correctly.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking the gray panel re-arms the grid, allowing multiple beam firings per attempt. The beam direction matches the last arrow pressed before clicking the white cells. FAILED: Clicking magenta dots does nothing. GOAL IS NOT: A single beam shot is required; you can fire repeatedly after resetting. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug and set beam direction. Clicking white cells fires the beam. Clicking the gray panel resets the grid to allow another shot.

GOAL: Move the plug to the socket by firing a beam to clear the gate. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug and set beam direction; clicks activate grid cells. RULE: Clicking the gray panel re-arms the grid, allowing multiple beam shots per attempt. TRAP: Assuming the grid fires only once; re-arming is essential for multi-stage paths.

GOAL: Navigate the block to the base and deliver the collected plus sign. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block one space per press. RULE: Success requires returning the item to the starting location, not just collecting it. TRAP: Believing the level ends immediately upon picking up the item, ignoring the need to transport it.

GOAL: Paint the grid with four colors using a rotating stamp and three liquid pours. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the view; clicks select tools; space applies the active tool. RULE: Liquids fill regions based on the current view angle, overwriting previous layers. TRAP: Assuming the diagonal stays hidden; pouring green revealed that it belongs to the lower-right region.

GOAL: Fit the block perfectly into the bottom gap. CONTROLS: Click bars for horizontal moves and stems for vertical drops. RULE: The piece must stop exactly where the gap ends, not overshoot. TRAP: Thinking the piece slides until blocked; it only moves as many steps as programmed.

GOAL: Clear the puzzle in just two clicks. CONTROLS: Clicking D1 adjusts the upper sections; clicking D2 shifts the lower sections. RULE: Only one action per click, and clicking a button that causes no change stops the game. TRAP: Thinking you need to click many times to push the plug right; the solution was surprisingly short.

GOAL: Guide the active tokens to their matching target cells. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected piece; clicking a piece selects it. RULE: Only the currently selected piece responds to movement commands. TRAP: Clicking an already-active piece does nothing; you must click the specific token you intend to move.

GOAL: Move fluid between five columns to match three target levels. CONTROLS: Click buttons to push fluid right or pull it left between adjacent columns. RULE: Each push transfers exactly two units, regardless of column width. TRAP: Assuming total volume is conserved; it is not, as transfers depend on source width.

GOAL: Move the large block to cover the white cross marker. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the block one step in that direction. RULE: The level ends when the block completely hides the target symbol. TRAP: Assuming the blue pattern was a target to fill, when it was just a wall.

ESTABLISHED: The box is trapped in the right room; the door is closed, blocking the player from reaching it. The box cannot physically move to the right hole due to corridor constraints. FAILED: Pushing the box right, moving the dot token, and assuming the box could reach the right hole. GOAL IS NOT: Placing the box in the right hole, as this is physically impossible. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; mouse clicks move the dot token between blocks but do not grab or reposition the box itself.

ESTABLISHED: The door retracts only while you stand on the marker; it closes the moment you step away. FAILED: Standing on the marker, moving away, and hoping the door stays open. It does not. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the exit before the door shuts, as the door is instant. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move. Space rewinds to the start; your abandoned body solidifies into a block once you leave that spot.

GOAL: Guide the plug to the head's interior. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug; panels trigger compression or clear. RULE: A beam blocked at zero distance triggers compression. TRAP: Hitting the red wall with the beam does nothing; it must hit the socket.

GOAL: Move two blocks to specific targets using directional inputs. CONTROLS: Arrows move blocks; inverted blocks move opposite to input. RULE: Blocks slide until hitting walls or other blocks, not just one space. TRAP: Assuming standard movement for inverted blocks; they require counter-intuitive input direction.

GOAL: Seat the plug into the ring’s hole. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected plug; clicks select a plug. RULE: Pushing a plug into a purple barrier teleports it to the matching socket side. TRAP: Assuming the left plug stays left; you must select the right plug to finish.

ESTABLISHED: The plug's white body spans ninety cells, and its two red tips are diagonally adjacent to this body. FAILED: Assuming any red group touching the body is a valid goal, which falsely includes the plug's own tips. GOAL IS NOT: The red cells that form the plug's current tip positions, as these are part of the tool, not the target. CONTROLS: Rotating the plug changes which red cells are considered its tips, thereby altering which remaining red groups count as valid goals.

GOAL: Move two blocks into matching holes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active block; clicking a block makes it active. RULE: Only the clicked block responds to arrows, so you must toggle control between blocks. TRAP: Thinking the frame blocks movement; it is passable, so do not avoid it.

GOAL: Clear the block by moving into it. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the square and drain the yellow bar. RULE: The bar empties after twenty moves, but you remain alive with no game over. TRAP: Thinking the empty bar causes death or consumes a life; it merely stops further moves.

GOAL: Merge scattered blocks into one shape using three clicks. CONTROLS: Click empty space to pull nearby pieces; click a piece to combine overlapping ones. RULE: Pieces move only if within a strict radius, preventing distant grabs. TRAP: Assuming Euclidean distance allows diagonal reach; the game likely uses Manhattan distance, making diagonal moves shorter than expected.
